consequence.statement: The max_transfer_retries setting, used to transfer chunks to new ingesters during rolling restarts, is removed; the Write Ahead Log (WAL) replaces it, so verify the WAL covers your rolling-restart use.

original.statement: The ingester setting max_transfer_retries (-ingester.max-transfer-retries) is removed in favor of the Write Ahead Log (WAL).

decision.reason: [ev-c6e07f70e7d9] says `max_transfer_retries` (`-ingester.max-transfer-retries`) is removed "in favor of the Write Ahead log (WAL)", and explains that it was used to transfer chunks to new ingesters during rolling restarts. That matches superseded-upstream: the setting is removed and another mechanism takes over its job. [ev-b19cd3bb8e8b] and [ev-8ec3d6c379c3] give the replacements: enable the WAL (preferred, with optional flush_on_shutdown) or flush manually through /shutdown?flush=true. The evidence never says that keeping the setting causes a failure, rejection or startup error, so a mandatory-work kind such as setting-ignored (P2's answer) would claim more than the evidence supports.
